 Presented by Mailbag: Adrian Peterson's Vikings Ring of Honor Weekend
 Nov 09, 2026 at 06:00 AM Craig Peters Editing Director & Quality Control
 Copied! 
 Alli Rusco/Minnesota Vikings Do you have a comment or question? Send it to the Mailbag. Every Monday we'll post several comments and/or questions. Click here   to submit a comment or question to Mailbag. Remember to include your name and town in the email. If Twitter / X is your jam, you can   send a question to me that way   as well. 
 It's not too often we get to start this post by me wishing everyone a "Happy Game Day," but such is the case.
 It's even rarer for an edition to occur on the same day as the formal induction of running back Adrian Peterson into the Vikings Ring of Honor.
 Given the set of circumstances, today's Mailbag will venture a little from the norm. We'll post another Mailbag on Tuesday (at some point in the afternoon) that will feature fan questions.
 Vikings.com/Adrian is a custom-built page featuring some of our team's latest content and some all-time great moments that showcase Peterson's path to a Purple Jacket and has him on trajectory to add a Gold Jacket with enshrinement in the Pro Football Hall of Fame as early as next year.
 Alli Rusco/Minnesota Vikings I sincerely recommend checking out that page if you haven't, because it will help pass the time while waiting on tonight's game between the Vikings (6-1) and Bills (6-1) to wrap Week 9 in a game broadcast nationally on ABC and ESPN. Kickoff is 7:15 p.m. (CT).
 For those who can't attend in person, Peterson's halftime Ring of Honor ceremony will be streamed live on Vikings.com and in the official Vikings App . 
 Tonight also will be Minnesota's annual Salute to Service home game, which pays tribute to veterans, active duty and reserve members of the military with multiple well-deserved recognitions.
 It's never lost on me that I get to do something I love so greatly because of the service and sacrifices of so many. This year's participants in the 10 th  annual Hy-Vee Veterans Voyage attended Sunday's walk-through at Twin Cities Orthopedics Performance Center. The participants met Peterson and current players after the practice and shared their personal stories that we'll relay in upcoming content.
 One such work-related opportunity I'll forever appreciate was being able to attend a ceremony honoring Peterson Sunday evening at TCO Performance Center.
 The Vikings welcomed Peterson's family, his coaches from youth and high school, Vikings Legends and Ring of Honor members and their family members.
 Adrian Peterson's Purple Jacket Ceremony Ahead of Ring of Honor Induction 
 View photos of Vikings Legend Adrian Peterson's Purple Jacket ceremony ahead of being inducted into the Vikings Ring of Honor.

 Each speaker shared thoughts about the way Peterson impacted them and locker rooms in Minnesota (Wilf and Felton), Seattle (Teasley) and Washington (O'Connell).
 Current players, including Myles Price, have talked about Peterson's impact on them, and I asked Peterson last week about what it means to him to have inspired this tier of players.
 "Yeah, it means a lot. It really means a lot. And that's what it's all about. Reach one, teach one," Peterson said. "And to know that a lot of those guys, I was a guy they looked up to, an idol, to put a word out there, as well, that I've heard, it's amazing, man. I played this game to be the best to ever do it and to inspire people.
 "When I was able to come up and talk to the rookies [this past summer], I was able to see how much I left for those guys to build off of. And that is one of the best feelings you can imagine because being out of the league for the time I've been out, I'm able to know and continue to be reminded that, you really impacted the game to the point where a lot of these guys who are coming into the league, you inspired their game, I'm sure along with other players, but you inspired them. You helped them get through adversity. You showed them the way to work, to prepare, the mindset to have, to overcome adversity, whether that's injuries or just life in general, understanding the source to go through to accomplish those things.
 "Anytime I see these youngsters and they are giving me praise and telling me how I inspired them or how they looked up to me, that's the job-well-done moment for me, so I always embrace it over any yard, any MVP or any big win, any record," Peterson continued. "For me, impacting the human spirit and inspiring youngsters or anyone in general to overcome, persevere, to be a better version of themselves, that's what life is about to me."
